title: Nonlinear Climate Resilience in Marine Capture Fisheries: Evidence From China and Norway
content:
ABSTRACT

Marine capture fisheries production (MCFP) is vulnerable to climate change, but the nonlinear relationship between climate and MCFP is not yet well understood across different national fisheries systems. Using annual data from China and Norway from 1961 to 2023, random forest (RF) models and partial-dependence plots are applied. Detrended production anomalies assess impact, recovery, and temporal variability. CO2 and surface air temperature (SAT) were the two leading predictors in both countries; in China, their ranks swapped across random seeds, while in Norway SAT consistently ranked first. At species level, CO2 and SAT were the leading predictors across the selected Chinese species and SAT across the selected Norwegian species, although relationship directions differed. China's upper–lower contrasts for CO2 and SAT are statistically supported in the primary analysis but approach zero following production-regime adjustment. Norway's upper–lower contrast confidence intervals include zero, and the estimated change points are imprecise in both countries. China has a positive mean event-year production shortfall, but its difference from other years is statistically uncertain. Recovery estimates depend on event definitions and regime adjustment. Norway's event estimates are generally uncertain, and its temporal-variability point estimate is higher in the main analysis, but the cross-country difference is statistically uncertain. Several findings are sensitive to detrending, fishing effort, and regime treatment. The results describe predictive associations rather than causal climate effects and support monitoring environmental conditions together with fishing pressure, catch composition, and long-term MCFP changes.
